Which inputs are switched off by another input, and at what value

Source: R/calculator.R
mm_calculator_gates.Rd

Some predictors only mean something when another one says so. A Step 2 score has no value for an applicant who has not sat Step 2, and a form that lets a reader say "not reported" and leave 250 in the box beside it is offering a combination the model was never fitted on: the model reads that as an applicant with the parked score plus the not-reported offset, which is not what the reader typed and not what they meant.

Usage

mm_calculator_gates(gates, model)

Arguments

gates

A named list, or NULL. Each name is a gated predictor and each element is a list with by, when, and optionally value.

model

A mm_model().

Value

The gates, normalised, with value and the controlling predictor's printed name filled in.

Details

So a gate names the controlling predictor, the level at which the gate closes, and the value the gated input takes while it is shut. The default value is the median the datadist recorded, which is where a parked value is usually put.
